svg.title: Module 13 one-page guide: Observability, Evaluation & Drift
svg.text: CSCI 391 · MODULE 13 · ONE-PAGE LECTURE GUIDE
Observability, Evaluation & Drift
Not just 'did it run and how fast?' — but 'did it behave correctly, why, and is it
drifting?'
Part IV · Hardening and Operations · Week 13 · Read: Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 14
OPENING CASE
Integration tests: categories handled, escalation honored, no competitor names — all green. Two weeks later: clipped,
dismissive replies to frustrated users. Three days to diagnose, because the team had success/failure logs and p50/p99
latency — but no record of what was retrieved, why a strategy was chosen, or how the reply scored on tone.
Agents fail semantically, not structurally. You need probabilistic quality
metrics, traces of every step, and baselines to compare against.
KEY FRAMEWORK
The agent observability stack
Span-based tracing across multi-step runs
(OpenTelemetry)
Structured logs of tool calls and token spend
LLM-as-judge evaluation of semantic quality
Regression suites and drift detection (3σ and CUSUM)
YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO
Instrument agent runs with OpenTelemetry traces and
spans
Define a production-ready structured logging schema
Build evaluation pipelines: baseline, gate, monitor,
shadow
Detect anomalies with the three-sigma rule and slow
drift with CUSUM
ENTERPRISE LENS · ADDISON BOYER
A spike in average cost per run is a leading indicator that behavior changed — often before quality metrics move.
Map every evaluation result to a trace ID. When a score drops, you should be one click from the exact run that
produced it.
Shadow-evaluate a candidate version on real traffic next to production before promoting it. Build baselines from a
known-good period, not a guess.
DISCUSS
→ Which quality metric would your users notice before your dashboard does?
→ How can CUSUM catch a gradual cost shift that a 3σ threshold misses?
Concepts after Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 14. Case framing, synthesis, and enterprise lens: Addison Boyer.
